articles.title: Região de Campinas: 1 a cada 4 veículos tem licenciamento vencimento | G1
articles.standfirst: Levantamento do Detran-SP aponta 617.857 documentos atrasados até setembro; infração gravíssima pode resultar em multa, pontos na CNH e remoção do veículo.
articles.summary: Levantamento do Detran-SP aponta 617.857 documentos atrasados até setembro; infração gravíssima pode resultar em multa, pontos na CNH e remoção do veículo.
articles.body:
Imagem de arquivo mostra carros trafegando em via de Campinas (SP). — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Cerca de um em cada quatro veículos da região de Campinas está com o licenciamento vencido, em média, segundo levantamento do Departamento Estadual de Trânsito de São Paulo (Detran-SP).

Os dados mostram que 617.857 veículos estavam com o documento em atraso até setembro deste ano, em uma frota ativa de 2.608.986 veículos. Na prática, os licenciamentos vencidos representam 23,7% da frota da região.

O número de licenciamentos vencidos registrado em nove meses em 2026 é o maior dos últimos cinco anos na série disponibilizada pelo Detran-SP. Ao mesmo tempo, a frota ativa da região cresceu de 2.364.035 veículos em 2022 para 2.608.986 em 2026, aumento de quase 245 mil veículos no período.

Licenciamentos na região de Campinas até setembro

O levantamento considera os licenciamentos de carros, motos e outros veículos com vencimento até setembro. Os dados de outubro, novembro e dezembro ficaram de fora porque, neste ano, os prazos ainda não venceram.

Os números podem incluir licenciamentos residuais de anos anteriores que continuam pendentes de pagamento, segundo o Detran-SP.

Circular com o licenciamento vencido é uma infração gravíssima, de acordo com o artigo 230 do Código de Trânsito Brasileiro (CTB).

A penalidade prevê multa de R$ 293,47, sete pontos na Carteira Nacional de Habilitação (CNH) e risco de remoção do veículo para o pátio.

Além da multa, o proprietário pode ter despesas adicionais com guincho, diárias de estadia no pátio, taxa de liberação do veículo e quitação dos débitos pendentes, como o próprio licenciamento, IPVA e eventuais multas.

Carros; veículos; trânsito em via de Campinas. — Foto: Reprodução/EPTV

Segundo o Detran-SP, a forma mais rápida de fazer o licenciamento é pelo portal do órgão.

Para concluir o procedimento, o proprietário deve quitar eventuais multas de trânsito e o IPVA, informar o número do Renavam e pagar a taxa de licenciamento, atualmente de R$ 174,08.

Após o pagamento, o Certificado de Registro e Licenciamento de Veículo em meio digital (CRLV-e) pode ser baixado pelos portais do Detran-SP, do Poupatempo e da Secretaria Nacional de Trânsito (Senatran), além dos aplicativos Detran-SP, Poupatempo Digital e CNH do Brasil.

O documento pode ser armazenado no celular ou impresso em papel comum. Segundo o Detran-SP, neste ano a atualização ocorre de forma instantânea após a compensação do pagamento.

O pagamento também pode ser feito por internet banking, aplicativos bancários, caixas eletrônicos e bancos conveniados.

Caso o licenciamento não apareça disponível para quitação, o proprietário deve verificar a existência de pendências, como multas, débitos tributários ou bloqueios administrativos e judiciais.

articles.title: Two old-school Japanese mobile games are shutting down over the PHP exploit.
articles.summary:
World Quest and Save My Demonic World have run for over a decade, but they’re built on older tech that the developers say can’t be updated to patch the apocalyptic PHP exploit disclosed this week. Because the vulnerability affects almost 20 years of PHP, big chunks of internet history are in danger of being lost. Per Kotaku:
> Many old websites and services that are no longer being actively updated (or may simply be too old to receive the update, as was the case for these two games) are now at risk of permanently going offline. Such an event would lock swathes of the old internet from public view, including bits that were already beginning to break down and become inaccessible.

articles.title: US weekly jobless claims near 57-year lows, underscore labor market stability
articles.summary: By Lucia Mutikani WASHINGTON, Oct 22 (Reuters) - The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits dropped to near 57-year lows last week a...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON, Oct 22 (Reuters) - The number of Americans filing new claims for unemployment benefits dropped to near 57-year lows last week amid low layoffs, suggesting a modest pickup in job growth in October after September's underwhelming performance.

The weekly jobless claims report from the Labor Department on Thursday, the most timely data on the economy's health, ‌continued to show no material stress in the labor market from the oil price shock stemming from the US-Israeli war with Iran.

Economists say strong growth in profits amid robust domestic demand, ‌and a smaller workforce against the backdrop of retirements and an immigration crackdown by the Trump administration, were shielding workers from layoffs.

There are, however, worries that tightening financial conditions and higher interest rates because of the drawn-out Middle East conflict could undercut ​the labor market next year.

"The administration's immigration policies may have tightened up the labor markets where companies are unable to find the help they need to produce their goods and services so they are holding tight to the workers they have," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. "Workers are suddenly irreplaceable in many industries."

Initial claims for state unemployment benefits fell 6,000 to a seasonally adjusted 194,000 for the week ended October 17. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast 200,000 claims for the latest week. It was the sixth consecutive week that claims remained at or below the 200,000 mark. Claims are within striking distance of the 189,000 level touched in mid-July, ‌which was the lowest reading since 1969.

The claims data covered the period ⁠during which the government surveyed business establishments for the nonfarm payrolls component of October's employment report. The four-week moving average of claims, seen as a better measure of labor market trends as it irons out week-to-week volatility, fell between the September and October survey weeks.

At face value that would suggest an improvement in payroll ⁠gains this month. Payrolls increased by 29,000 jobs in September after rebounding by 133,000 in August. Payrolls tend to underperform when Labor Day falls relatively late in the month as was the case in September. Economists continue to view the labor market as still in a "low-hire, low-fire" state.

But uncertainty from the war and tariffs on imports has stymied hiring. Stocks on Wall Street were trading lower. The dollar was little changed against a basket of currencies. US ​Treasury ​yields fell.

articles.title: OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia had record lobbying quarters
articles.summary: Leading AI companies are ramping up their federal lobbying spending, with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Nvidia having their biggest lobbying quarters yet ahead of the midterms.
articles.body: It was a busy summer for AI lobbyists. Anthropic, OpenAI, and Nvidia each had their highest-spending lobbying quarter between July and September, federal disclosures show. Nvidia spent the most of the group at $2.2 million, followed by Anthropic’s $2.1 million and OpenAI’s $1.5 million. Compared to other Big Tech companies with long-established presences in Washington, the sums aren’t out of the ordinary. Microsoft, for example, has spent at least $2 million a quarter going back to 2021, and Google regularly spends over $3 million, including this quarter. But it’s a clear signal that the three AI firms recognize how important shaping policy has become. Tech CEOs were already visible fixtures in Washington during this period, with many of them attending a White House lunch with President Donald Trump in late September, which resulted in a “morally binding” AI safety accord that they agreed to. The lobbying disclosures show that even more discussions were happening frequently behind the scenes, during a time just before Trump named his AI czar and task force. With Democrats expected to win back at least some control in Congress after this year’s midterm elections, AI companies may only find it more important to engage with lawmakers who see cracking down on the industry as a winning issue. Anthropic included a detailed list of bills, executive orders, and other topics it lobbied Congress and the White House about in the third quarter. Among them were AI-related provisions in the Kids Online Safety Act (KOSA), export control provisions in the AI Overwatch Act, Trump’s executive order renaming AI “Super Intelligence,” and the Ratepayer Protection Act, which aims to put energy costs for data centers on their developers. OpenAI’s lobbying looks like a response to some of the fallout from the Hugging Face attack, though the disclosures only list high-level topics. In addition to engaging on issues like copyright, OpenAI lobbied Congress, the White House, the Small Business Administration, and the Commerce and State Departments over cybersecurity evaluations for frontier models, AI safety oversight frameworks, and antitrust protections for information sharing. Nvidia lobbied Congress, as well as several different federal agencies and White House offices, on issues including 6G networks, “responsible AI design,” competition policy, quantum computing, and export control policy. Apple also had a record-breaking quarter, spending $3.1 million and engaging on issues including intellectual property, tariffs, kids online safety, competition, and domestic semiconductor manufacturing. It engaged on bills that seek to put the onus on app stores to verify users’ ages, for example. It’s the first quarter in which Apple has reported spending more than $3 million on lobbying. The disclosures show that leading AI companies are becoming increasingly active in policymaking, in a quarter that marks a lead-up to the midterm elections. OpenAI didn’t even spend $1 million on lobbying in a single quarter until this year, and didn’t spend more than half a million until the end of 2024. The most Anthropic spent in a single quarter last year was just over $1 million. And this quarter is the first in which Nvidia has spent more than $2 million. With issues like data center development and AI safety on many voters’ minds, AI lobbyists’ work will likely only increase no matter whichever party has control next year.

articles.title: AI agents are causing massive headaches for banks.
articles.summary:
According to Axios, banks have detected AI agents accessing customer accounts and taking actions, sometimes without clear authorization or instruction. JPMorgan, Citi, Bank of America, and Morgan Stanley have started to restrict or block some third-party access because of it. But more concerning, it seems the banks just don’t know what AI agents are doing or why:
> One bank executive told Axios they struggle to differentiate between agents, as well as whether an agent has been authorized by a user or has gone rogue and gained access to a customer account.

articles.title: Google’s AI overview led some people to think they were donating to James Talarico when they weren’t.
articles.summary:
Instead, their money went to a political action committee that funneled the money to the reelection campaign of Colorado’s Democratic Senator John Hickenlooper. According to The Atlantic:
> The mix-up wasn’t all AI’s fault. The link led to a misleading donation page that carried Talarico’s name and picture, and specified only at the bottom that the money would go to Hickenlooper. But Google’s AI tool evidently didn’t read the fine print. And perhaps no one would have clicked on it had Google not highlighted the page in an authoritative-sounding AI response.

articles.title: The disastrous PHP vulnerabilities were exploited days before the patch
articles.summary: A hacker attempted to exploit the PHP bug that impacted sites across the web four days before a patch was released, according to Amazon Threat Intelligence.
articles.body: Hackers attempted to exploit the PHP flaws impacting sites across the web days before they were patched, according to a report from Amazon Threat Intelligence. CJ Moses, Amazon chief information security officer, writes that the company’s security team found a PHP2Shell exploit attempt on October 17th through a monitoring system designed to bait hackers, as reported earlier by Wired and Bleeping Computer. On Wednesday, websites scrambled to apply a patch for two critical security vulnerabilities affecting PHP, a programming language used by a large portion of the internet, including WordPress sites. The flaws — CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 — could allow hackers to execute malicious code remotely on vulnerable devices. Elizabeth Barron, the PHP Foundation’s executive director, tells The Verge that “to our knowledge, there has been no successful attempt at remote code execution” but stresses that updating affected systems is “imperative.” The PHP Foundation initially theorized the bug in 2024, and while its security team came up with potential solutions, a fix was delayed due to “backward compatibility breaks, new denial-of-service potential, or requiring changes to many third-party extensions which seemed impossible to coordinate.” As the PHP Foundation prepared to ship the fix this week, details about the bugs began trickling out on forums and social media, with some security firms releasing information about them before the official release. But the report from Amazon Threat Intelligence suggests a bad actor may have identified the vulnerability before details started leaking. “While the vulnerability was under embargo, the targeting of a honeypot from an anonymized IP address suggests the activity was conducted by a threat actor, though it remains unclear how the actor acquired exploit information prior to disclosure,” Moses writes. Amazon Threat Intelligence discovered several other exploitation attempts on October 21st in the hours before the patch’s release. “We are confident that a serious vulnerability with a fix stuck on hard trade-offs would now reach the PHP Foundation leadership much sooner, as we’re changing processes so leadership can help steer the situation to a timely resolution,” the PHP Foundation says. “We are now prioritizing measures to make sure vulnerabilities that need similarly complex fixes get resolved faster when they are reported in the future.”

articles.title: Rhode Island is suing Meta for turning a blind eye to scam ads.
articles.summary:
The state’s Attorney General Peter Neronha filed the suit in Providence Superior Court, accusing Meta of making billions in profits from scam ads, while simultaneously telling users it was working hard to protect them. The suit cites reporting on leaked Meta documents from Reuters that said:
> … it was earning ​far more from high-risk scam ads than it expected to pay in fines for allowing them.
> According to those documents, Meta displays around 15 billion “higher risk” scam ads to users every day, and earned roughly ​10% of its 2024 revenue from fraudulent e-commerce, dubious health products and other banned marketing.
